title: C-DAC PG Diplomas
kicker: Short full-time post-graduate diplomas in computing and electronics

value.body: The Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, runs full-time post-graduate diploma courses through its training centres and authorised partner institutes. Courses include PG-DAC (Advanced Computing), PG-DESD (Embedded Systems Design), PG-DVLSI (VLSI Design), PG-DBDA (Big Data Analytics) and PG-DAI (Artificial Intelligence). They are intensive, job-oriented diplomas, not university degrees.

items.label: Batches
items.note: Commonly starting around February and August; check the current calendar

items.label: Entrance test
items.note: C-DAC's Common Admission Test; the sections you take depend on the courses you choose

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A B.E. / B.Tech in a listed branch (such as CS, IT, electronics, electrical or instrumentation), an MCA, or a relevant M.Sc; each course lists its own eligible degrees. Register for C-CAT, take the sections required for your chosen courses, and then choose a centre and course in the counselling rounds based on your rank. Final-year students have been allowed to apply, subject to the notice.

value.title: At a glance
items: It is a diploma, not a master's degree, so it does not replace an M.Tech for posts that ask for one.
Centres offer placement support, but jobs are not guaranteed and outcomes vary by centre, course and batch.
Fees and the courses on offer differ between centres; check each centre's listing.
The pace is fast, with long daily lab hours over the six months.
